modern: We ought to consider not only that our life is wasting away day by day and a smaller part of it is left, but another thing must also be taken into account: that if a man should live longer, it is quite uncertain whether the understanding will still be adequate for grasping things, and keep the power of contemplation which strives to gain knowledge of the divine and the human. For if he begins to fall into senility, perspiration and nutrition and imagination and appetite, and whatever else there is of the kind, will not fail; but the power of making use of ourselves, and filling up the measure of our duty, and clearly distinguishing all appearances, and considering whether a man should now leave life, and whatever else of the kind absolutely requires a disciplined reason—all this is already extinguished. We must hurry, then, not only because we are nearer to death every day, but also because the conception and understanding of things cease first.
original: We ought to consider not only that our life is daily wasting away and a smaller part of it is left, but another thing also must be taken into the account, that if a man should live longer, it is quite uncertain whether the understanding will still continue sufficient for the comprehension of things, and retain the power of contemplation which strives to acquire the knowledge of the divine and the human. For if he shall begin to fall into dotage, perspiration and nutrition and imagination and appetite, and whatever else there is of the kind, will not fail; but the power of making use of ourselves, and filling up the measure of our duty, and clearly separating all appearances, and considering whether a man should now depart from life, and whatever else of the kind absolutely requires a disciplined reason,—all this is already extinguished. We must make haste, then, not only because we are daily nearer to death, but also because the conception of things and the understanding of them cease first.
